answer.rationale: Competitor price pressure on SMB base creates immediate churn risk. Memory_73 shows targeted promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. Memory_57 confirms referral incentives work well but only on established accounts (6+ months); this doesn't help retain churning new/mid-tenure SMBs facing price pressure today. Memory_86 (onboarding simplification) and activation_messaging improve adoption friction, not price-sensitivity. Enterprise_sales_assist addresses wrong segment. Promotional pricing is the direct countermeasure: it addresses the stated driver (price sensitivity), targets the affected cohort (SMB), and has validated precedent. Risk: margin compression and potential anchoring effect if not time-bounded. Mitigation: run as time-limited experiment (30-day window) with clear sunset, monitor for actual retention lift vs. pure discount-driven behavior, reserve option to combine with referral incentives on retained accounts. Confidence tempered by: (1) this is a reactive move under time pressure, (2) we cannot re-verify memory_73 today, (3) promotional pricing sustainability depends heavily on execution details not yet specified.
